issues.description: Method mismatch: Animal.messageOnFeed() return type. Problem statement (UML and task text) specifies an abstract method Animal.messageOnFeed() that returns a String. The solution repository defines the method signature as public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java and provides a new FeedResponse class; Pig and Seal implementations also return FeedResponse. This inconsistency forces students to choose between implementing messageOnFeed() to return String (as described in the exercise text and UML) or to return FeedResponse (as in the provided solution), which causes compilation/test failures and unclear expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnFeed() return type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred simple fix: change the solution to match the problem statement (option A). Update src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to declare public abstract String messageOnFeed(); update Pig, Seal, Goat to return the specified String messages (e.g. "Oink!", "Arf Arf!", "Maah!"). Remove the FeedResponse class and adjust any code that constructs or expects FeedResponse (e.g. Farm.feedAllAnimals() should print the returned String). Alternatively (if keeping FeedResponse is desired), update the problem statement, UML, and template to document FeedResponse and require messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse, but the recommended action is to adopt Strings to match the exercise text and UML.

issues.description: The exercise specification (UML and task text) defines an abstract method Animal.messageOnFeed() with return type String, but the provided solution changes the API by adding a new type FeedResponse and declaring Animal.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. Specifically: the problem statement UML declares messageOnFeed(): String (problem_statement.md), the task text instructs students to implement messageOnFeed() as an abstract method returning a String (problem_statement.md), while the solution introduces FeedResponse (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/FeedResponse.java) and declares Animal.messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java). Additionally, individual implementations in the solution are inconsistent (Seal and Pig return FeedResponse, but Goat implements messageOnFeed() returning String), which further increases confusion. Students following the problem text will implement messageOnFeed() to return String and will be blocked by the solution/reference using FeedResponse and by the solution's own internal inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API between problem statement and solution. Two clear options: (A) Revert the solution to match the specification: change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String, update Seal and Pig to return String values (remove FeedResponse class and its usages), and update any code in the solution that expects FeedResponse accordingly; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to explicitly introduce the FeedResponse type and change the required signature to messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse (document FeedResponse fields and how its message should be used/printed in recipes such as singFarmSong()). Whichever approach is chosen, ensure all solution implementations consistently use the same signature (no mixed String/FeedResponse implementations) and update examples and tests to reflect the chosen API.
